[Textbook misprint: the line is printed with a spurious \(\cdot\) (dot) between the two vectors instead of \(=\); it is solved as the intended line \(\bar{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-6\hat{k})\). Only the line's direction affects the angle.]

The angle \(\theta\) between a line with direction \(\bar{b}\) and a plane with normal \(\bar{n}\) is
\(\sin\theta=\dfrac{|\bar{b}\cdot\bar{n}|}{|\bar{b}||\bar{n}|}.\)

Here \(\bar{b}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-6\hat{k}=(2,3,-6)\) and the plane \(\bar{r}\cdot(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})=0\) has normal \(\bar{n}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}=(2,-1,1).\)

\(\bar{b}\cdot\bar{n}=(2)(2)+(3)(-1)+(-6)(1)=4-3-6=-5.\)
\(|\bar{b}|=\sqrt{2^2+3^2+(-6)^2}=\sqrt{49}=7,\quad |\bar{n}|=\sqrt{2^2+(-1)^2+1^2}=\sqrt{6}.\)

\(\sin\theta=\dfrac{|-5|}{7\cdot\sqrt{6}}=\dfrac{5}{7\sqrt{6}}=\dfrac{5\sqrt{6}}{42}.\)

\(\therefore\ \theta=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{5}{7\sqrt{6}}\right)=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{5\sqrt{6}}{42}\right)\) is the required acute angle.
